lessons: Unscheduled jobs dominate cost (150×priority each; the champion's 10–15 unscheduled jobs cost 1500–3000 on the worst days), so the highest-leverage change is scheduling more jobs before polishing travel or lateness.

The promoted change simply traded a low-priority job for a higher-priority one, confirming that deliberately dropping cheap priority-1/2 jobs to fit priority-3/5 jobs is profitable because the unscheduled penalty is 150×priority.

Pure re-sequencing/2-opt (1450.8), load-balancing (1370.5), earliest-emergency-start (1398.5) and naive local search (1390.5) all scored worse than the champion, so the remaining cost is not in travel or load balancing but in coverage.
Agent 2 crashed two days with 'Set changed size during iteration': never insert/remove while looping over a live set/list — materialize the candidate sequence in a new list and assign afterward.

Local-search moves that look travel-positive can be net-negative because each job changing tech costs 20; every move's delta must include 20×(jobs moved) plus the 150×priority impact on unscheduled jobs.
strategies: Coverage-first construction: sort open jobs by descending priority (5→1) and insert each at the best feasible position across all healthy techs, using route_cost; only leave a job unscheduled if no insertion fits within the overtime cap.

Generalize the champion's bump rule: when a priority-3/5 job has no feasible insertion, remove from one tech the job with the smallest (150×its_priority - saved travel/lateness by dropping it) and retry inserting the high-priority job.

Respect overtime exactly: after each route is built, run route() or drop_until_feasible per tech so end ≤ shift_end + max_overtime, then try to re-insert any dropped job on another tech rather than discarding it.

Treat emergencies as hard constraints but budget their response wait: assign each emergency to a feasible tech, and only accept extra wait if it avoids dropping jobs whose 150×priority penalty is larger than the wait difference.

Add a bounded (≤1s) local search of relocate/swap moves accepted only when the full checker-style cost (travel + priority×lateness + overtime + 150×unscheduled + 20×moved + emergency wait) strictly improves.
Avoid mutation-during-iteration bugs by building every candidate sequence in a fresh list and replacing plan entries only after the loop finishes; never modify the collection you are iterating over.
Score candidate plans with the exact cost formula rather than a proxy (e.g. minimizing route_cost alone will miss the 150×priority unscheduled penalty), and return the best feasible candidate.

Use morning_tech as a tiebreaker: prefer keeping a job with its original tech unless the gain clearly exceeds the 20-point churn penalty, so the plan does not pay move costs for marginal travel savings.

lessons: The wait-budgeting emergency policy (agent 3, 1315.9) beat the old champion by 48.2 points, showing emergency response wait is cheap enough to trade for preserving jobs with 150×priority penalties.

Unscheduled jobs still dominate the new champion: 15 unscheduled on day 4 and 11 on day 26 imply roughly 1650–2250+ penalty before travel, so next round must prioritize scheduling one more job over polishing travel or lateness.

Coverage-first priority-descending insertion (agent 0, 1344.4) also beat the old champion, confirming that scheduling high-priority jobs early is the reliable base, but it needs wait-aware emergency handling to match the promoted policy.

Overtime cleanup/reinsertion and anti-mutation fixes (agents 2 and 5, 1370.5 and 1383.8) scored below the old champion, so feasibility bookkeeping alone does not help unless it directly converts an unscheduled job into a scheduled one.

Naive full-cost local search (agent 4, 1364.5) only tied the old champion, so any local search must be seeded from the new wait-aware construction and include the 20-move penalty plus 150×priority unscheduled effects.

Before optimizing travel, explicitly count and minimize unscheduled jobs: schedule every priority-3/5 job first, then fit priority-2/1 jobs, because dropping a p5 costs 750 and a p1 costs 150.

When a high-priority job has no feasible insertion, extend the bump rule: remove the job minimizing (150×its_priority + its route/lateness contribution - emergency-wait increase it causes), then retry the insertion.
Treat max_overtime as usable budget: accept overtime minutes to schedule a job when its 150×priority penalty exceeds the extra overtime cost; do not drop it merely to end exactly at shift_end.

Re-insert any job dropped by overtime or bumping onto a different healthy tech immediately, in descending priority order, before considering it unscheduled.
Assign emergencies to feasible techs by minimizing added full objective cost, not just earliest start, so a tech already near a high-priority cluster is not forced to abandon it.
Keep mutation safety: build each candidate sequence in a fresh list and replace the plan only after evaluation, never modifying a list or set being iterated.

Plain coverage-first insertion passes on top of the exact-delta seed (agents 0 and 3) gained exactly 0 over the champion, so the residual 10–14 unscheduled jobs are not reachable by simple insertion — bumping already-scheduled low-value jobs is the missing mechanism.
Cross-tech reassignment still loses (agent 4, 1249.9) and the champion only shows moved 1–3, so the 20-per-move penalty plus added travel/overtime almost always outweighs the marginal coverage gain.

"""Round-0 seed policy: what a busy human dispatcher does.

Everyone keeps their remaining jobs. Each orphaned job (from the sick tech) and each
emergency goes to the nearest healthy tech with the right skill: emergencies to the
front of that tech's list, other jobs to the end. If that would push the tech past the
overtime limit, the job is left for tomorrow; an emergency instead bumps that
tech's lowest-priority jobs to tomorrow.
"""

from dispatchiq.helpers import drop_until_feasible, route, travel_min


def replan(state):
    plan = {t["id"]: ([] if t["sick"] else list(t["remaining"])) for t in state["techs"]}
    healthy = [t for t in state["techs"] if not t["sick"]]
    orphans = [j for t in state["techs"] if t["sick"] for j in t["remaining"]]
    emergencies = [jid for jid, j in state["jobs"].items() if j["emergency"]]
    for jid in emergencies + orphans:
        job = state["jobs"][jid]
        options = sorted((travel_min(state, t["loc"], job["loc"]), t["id"]) for t in healthy
                         if job["skill"] in t["skills"])
        for _, tid in options:
            tech = next(t for t in healthy if t["id"] == tid)
            seq = [jid] + plan[tid] if job["emergency"] else plan[tid] + [jid]
            if job["emergency"]:
                seq, _ = drop_until_feasible(state, tech, seq)  # bump routine jobs to tomorrow
            if route(state, tech, seq)["feasible"]:
                plan[tid] = seq
                break
    return plan
